title: Ancient Trees in the Czech Republic: Cities to Explore
meta_description: Prague's thickest protected tree is seven and a half metres round, and its best known story is almost certainly false. 13 places, 42 trees.
intro: The thickest protected tree in Prague measures seven and a half metres around, and the story everyone tells about it, that Beethoven sat beneath it, is almost certainly false. The city's register says as much rather than repeating it, which sets the tone for the rest. Prague dates its trees in ranges and admits where two records disagree by eighty years, as they do for the ginkgo in Stromovka. Brno keeps its own list: the Bystrc Lime, past 400 years old, survived a 1933 fire when a neighbour tried to smoke a marten out of its hollow trunk by setting it alight. Cesky Krumlov's oldest tree turns the usual pattern round: it is the free one, a village-square lime older than the paid monastery lindens nearby. Beyond the three cities, ten single-tree villages carry the country's national Tree of the Year winners: Teleci's hollow lime a person can stand inside, Rimov's pilgrimage linden that once held 51 people inside its trunk at once, a hamlet ash growing through the foundations of a German village emptied after the war, and a dying beech in Msecke Zehrovice the municipality has chosen not to save. Thirteen places, 42 trees mapped so far.
